questions.qtext: What is the main property of the diagonal matrix Σ in Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)?

options.text: It contains the eigenvalues of the matrix.
It contains the singular values of the matrix.
It represents the eigenvectors of the matrix.
It represents the null space of the matrix.

questions.solution:
(b)
The diagonal matrix Σ in Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) contains the singular values of the matrix A. These singular values are non-negative and represent the scale factors for the corresponding directions in the transformation.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: What is the relationship between the singular values and the eigenvalues of a matrix?

options.text: Singular values are always equal to eigenvalues.
Singular values are the square roots of the eigenvalues.
Singular values are the reciprocals of the eigenvalues.
Singular values are related to eigenvalues but not necessarily equal to them.

questions.solution:
(d)
While there is a relationship between singular values and eigenvalues, they are not necessarily equal. For symmetric matrices, the singular values are equal to the absolute values of the eigenvalues.

questions.qtext: What do eigenvectors do not represent in the context of matrices?

options.text: Vectors that transform a matrix into its inverse
Vectors that span the null space of the matrix
Vectors that remain in the same direction after transformation by the matrix
Vectors that are orthogonal to each other

questions.solution:
(a, b, d)
Eigenvectors are vectors that, when transformed by a matrix, only scale but do not change direction, except possibly by a scalar factor.

questions.qtext: In Gaussian elimination, what is not the purpose of row operations?

options.text: To find the determinant of the matrix
To convert the matrix into row-echelon form

questions.solution:
(c)
Row operations in Gaussian elimination are performed to transform the matrix into row-echelon form, facilitating further analysis and solving of systems of equations.

questions.qtext: If a matrix has distinct eigenvalues, what can be said about its eigenvectors?

options.text: They are orthogonal to each other

questions.solution:
(a)
If a matrix has distinct eigenvalues, then its corresponding eigenvectors are guaranteed to be linearly independent.

questions.qtext: In a system of linear equations, if the determinant of the coefficient matrix is zero, what can be said about the system?

options.text: The system has a unique solution
The system has infinitely many solutions
The system may or may not have a solution

questions.solution:
(c)
If the determinant of the coefficient matrix is zero, it implies that the system either has no solution or infinitely many solutions, but it cannot have a unique solution.
